name: Public procurement and tendering
one_line: The contracting authority's own custody of one regulated competitive purchase: the published notice, the tender documents it issued, the sealed bids it received from competitors it does not control, the moderated evaluation, the approval, the award and the standstill and debrief correspondence that follow. It is not activated by procurement vocabulary, a tender reference token, a portal name or a public body's name, and it is not the supplier's copy of the same bytes. Its increment over the government default is the fan-in of third-party sealed submissions plus the publication-and-remedy artifacts that only a regulated competition produces, and a sensitivity posture that is mixed within a single group rather than flat. Absorbs the legacy row gov.contract-award-record.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: the `government` schema declares no field rows (PR-6), so nothing below licenses a procurement fact. Every signal must evidence the holder as the CONTRACTING AUTHORITY running the competition, not as a bidder, a market watcher, or the eventual supplier. Where only one side's paperwork is present and the direction is unresolved, abstain.

a published notice in structured notice form — a contracting-authority block, a notice reference, a classification code block, a named regulated procedure (open, restricted, competitive dialogue, negotiated, light-touch, framework call-off), an estimated value slot and a fixed submission deadline — held together with the tender documents that the same notice points at

an issued tender pack whose volumes separate instructions to tenderers, specification or requirement schedule, pricing schedule, and draft contract terms, and whose instructions carry a timetable, a submission-format rule, exclusion or selection grounds and published award criteria with weightings; the weightings being fixed and published is the regime marker, not the criteria themselves

a clarification log with numbered questions, receipt dates, issued answers and an issued-to-all-tenderers column; simultaneous disclosure to every competitor is a duty artifact with no private-sourcing counterpart

a submission receipt register generated by a procurement portal on the authority's side — bidder reference, timestamped receipt, integrity hash, and a before-or-after-deadline flag — showing custody of sealed bids that the holder did not author

two or more complete submissions from DIFFERENT external organisations, all responding to the same issued pack under the same reference, present in one place; a single response is a supplier's own file, and the fan-in is what distinguishes buyer-side custody

a moderated evaluation record: criteria columns matching the published weightings, individual and consensus score rows keyed to bidder references, moderator narrative, and an evaluator declaration-of-interest sheet naming panel members against bidders

an award recommendation carrying an internal approval or delegated-authority signature block, followed by outbound decision correspondence to named unsuccessful organisations that discloses the winning tenderer, the recipient's own scores and a standstill or remedy window

a contract award notice in the same structured notice form as the opening notice, published after the decision and naming supplier and value — evidence only when it sits with the competition file that produced it, never alone

a procurement email or calendar record whose structured sender, recipient, organizer, attendee or subject slots carry an exact issued-pack reference AND cross the authority-to-bidder boundary in the authority's direction (procurement mailbox as recipient of clarifications, as organizer of a bid opening or site visit, as sender of an issued answer)
an export or archive manifest whose member paths repeatedly encode one competition reference across issued, received, evaluated and awarded families; manifests are inspected without unpacking
needs_llm: deciding DIRECTION OF CUSTODY when the tender reference, the specification text and the deadline appear identically on the authority's copy and the bidder's copy; only the surrounding population — one response versus many, receipt register versus submission confirmation, approval block versus internal bid/no-bid note — settles it, and it must be settled from a bounded local dossier

separating a regulated public competition from a private organisation's RFP that has copied the same furniture (timetable, weighted criteria, clarification window) but has no notice, no procedure name, no publication and no standstill

separating a purchase from a grant where the call, the received submissions and the scoresheet are structurally identical; the instrument at the end decides — a specification with deliverables and acceptance versus funding for the recipient's own purposes

recognizing an unlabeled internal document — a market-engagement note, a business case, a route-to-market options paper, a debrief script, a lessons-learned note — whose procurement function is expressed only in prose
deciding whether a mixed archive is one competition's file or a procurement team's whole year, and refusing to invent a competition where a forward pipeline register lists many

judging whether a body that runs a regulated competition is inside the state at all — a state-owned operator, a utility, a university, an arm's-length company and a charity buying under a funder's conditions all issue notice-shaped packs
abstaining whenever direction, instrument or body cannot be evidenced; “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: the words tender, bid, ITT, RFP, RFQ, RFI, procurement, sourcing, supplier, lot, framework, award, evaluation or contract in a filename, heading or folder name; every one of them appears on the supplier's copy of the same competition

a competition reference token (ITT-, RFP-, notice- or contract-number shaped) alone — the reference is printed on the authority's pack, on every bidder's response, on the published notice, and in press coverage; it identifies the competition, never the holder
a contracting authority's name, crest, letterhead, footer, PDF producer string or document-author metadata alone; the authority is the counterparty on every bidder's disk
a procurement portal's name, domain, watermark or notification-email template alone; the same portal serves buyers and bidders and sends both a submission confirmation and a receipt register
a commercial-in-confidence, restricted, or confidentiality legend alone; the legend is applied by the party who wrote the document and appears on both sides

a downloaded contract notice, prior-information notice, award notice, framework agreement or published specification kept for market scanning; publication by an authority is not custody by an authority
a single tender response, however complete, and however much of the authority's specification it quotes back
a purchase order, invoice, delivery note, receipt or payment record naming a public body; these are transactional records of a supply relationship, not the competition that created it
a parent folder named Tenders, Bids, Procurement, Contracts, Suppliers or Sourcing alone
a file extension or source_type alone; the design says to “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”
a shared download session or portal batch; “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
missing EXIF or dense OCR as proof that an image is a portal receipt screenshot; “the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot”

work_types: market engagement, prior-information notice, business case, or route-to-market options paper
contract notice, selection questionnaire, shortlisting record, or standstill of a restricted stage
invitation to tender pack: instructions to tenderers, specification, pricing schedule, draft terms
clarification question log and issued answers
bid receipt register, sealed-bid custody record, or late-submission record
received tender: technical response, pricing response, certificates, insurances, personnel evidence
individual score sheet, consensus or moderation record, evaluator declaration of interest
award recommendation report, internal approval, or delegated-authority decision
standstill letter, unsuccessful-bidder debrief, successful-bidder notification
contract award notice, transparency publication, or contracts-register entry
procurement challenge, remedies correspondence, or review response
framework establishment, mini-competition, direct award justification, or call-off
post-award contract mobilisation handover, procurement lessons-learned, or pipeline forward plan
grouping_reasons: one competition, bounded by an exact issued-pack or notice reference that appears in the authority's own issued documents and in the receipt register; this is the only anchor strong enough to admit a third-party submission into the group

a received-submissions fan-in that is content-incoherent but purpose-coherent — a pricing workbook, insurance certificates, CVs, a method statement and a signed form from one bidder cohere only because they were submitted to one call, which is the design's purpose-over-topic case

an issued-versus-received split inside the same competition: the authority's own pack and the competitors' responses must remain distinguishable, because collapsing them destroys the direction evidence that activated the row in the first place

an evaluation family bound to the same reference — individual sheets, consensus sheet, moderator notes, declarations — which must not be joined across competitions merely because the same evaluators recur
a decision-and-publication tail — recommendation, approval, notifications, standstill letters, award notice — bound by the same reference; publication of the award does not retro-publish the group
an export or archive manifest for one competition, kept shallow until access boundaries are known and never unpacked merely to strengthen recognition
duplicate and version families remain universal; issued pack v1, v2 and the addendum are a version family and acquire no procurement facts from neighbourhood

no group is a valid outcome for a standalone published notice or award notice; “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”
a forward pipeline register or contracts register lists many competitions and is a member of none; it must not donate a competition fact to any file it names

template.why: Empty by contract, not by judgement: the `government` schema declares no field rows under PR-6 (D1's deferral stands), and a template cannot branch on undeclared fields. The world does have an order, and it is recorded here as prose only — the bounded competition first, then the issued-versus-received-versus-decided function, then work type. Bidder identity must never become a folder level: a visible branch per losing organisation publishes, in the filesystem, exactly the fact the standstill and debrief regime keeps bilateral. Time is not first because “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders,” and a competition routinely straddles a year boundary between notice and award. Any later order remains the user's: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The same reference-timetable-criteria-evaluation-award shape occurs on both sides, and the shared fixture is the issued tender pack: ITT-2026-0412 Volume 1 - Instructions to Tenderers.docx is byte-identical in kind to a private company's RFP with weighted criteria and a clarification window. The discriminator is the regulated-competition apparatus, not the buyer's sector: this row requires publication and remedy artifacts that a private buyer never produces — a structured contract notice with a named regulated procedure, answers issued to all tenderers, a standstill or debrief letter disclosing the winner and the recipient's scores, or a published award notice; business_operations.procurement-sourcing requires a private organisation's own sourcing, free to negotiate, change criteria or cancel without notifying anyone. In the other direction, a supplier's single tender response — ITT-2026-0412 - our tender response - FINAL.docx — belongs to business_operations.procurement-sourcing's neighbourhood and never here, however completely it quotes the authority's pack. Neither side may activate from procurement vocabulary or a reference token alone. Provenance: inference.

The shared fixture is the executed agreement and its order form: Framework Schedule 4 - Order Form - Managed Print.docx sits on the authority's disk and on the supplier's disk as the same document. The discriminator is which lifecycle the surrounding population evidences: this row requires the COMPETITION that preceded signature — received bids from competitors, moderated evaluation, approval, standstill — and stops at award; business_operations.contract-administration requires the running of the agreement afterwards — a contracts register, notice calendar, variation and obligation tracking — and holds one agreement among many with no competition attached. A file that is only an executed contract activates neither by itself. Provenance: inference.

Reciprocal to the boundary that row already authored against this one, and named on the same fixture: an evaluation or assessment scoresheet whose rows are submission references and whose columns are criteria and named assessors — ITT-2026-0412 - Evaluation Consensus Scoresheet.xlsx here, Grant Call GC-2026-08 - Assessment Panel Scoresheet.xlsx there — is structurally identical on both sides. The discriminator is the instrument, not the process: this row requires the authority to be BUYING for itself, evidenced by a specification, priced schedule, deliverables and acceptance; grant-programme administration requires an instrument giving money for the recipient's own purposes under conditions with recovery on breach. Where only the scoresheet survives and no instrument is present, neither row activates. Provenance: inference.

The shared fixture is a package bid analysis: a spreadsheet of competing prices from named trade contractors against a common scope, with a recommendation. The discriminator is the buyer's constitution and the scope's anchor: this row requires a contracting authority's notice, procedure and publication or remedy trail; construction_property.subcontract requires a main contractor letting a works package on a named site under a main-contract reference, with no notice and no standstill. An authority procuring construction works sits here and produces both shapes, so the site-and-package anchor alone must not steal it, and the notice-and-procedure anchor alone must not steal a private main contractor's package tender. Provenance: inference.

also_holds_with.signal: An award recommendation, a standstill letter, an executed contract or a procurement challenge response is legitimately both a competition member and a legal instrument or correspondence. Coactivation is permitted and neither schema erases the other; Legal must not be used to conclude validity, breach, remedy entitlement or whether a challenge would succeed.

falls_through_to.when: a received tender, a receipt register, an evaluation or moderation record, an evaluator declaration, a standstill or debrief letter, or bidder correspondence has no accepted competition group; the harm avoided is disclosing which organisations bid, which lost, and what was said about them, all of which is third-party commercial information held in trust
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a published contract notice or award notice, a standalone issued specification, a certificate or a form has a durable purpose but no accepted competition group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: notices, tender packs, award notices or procurement guidance were downloaded for market scanning or reference with no evidenced role on either side
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: a procurement-shaped artifact is readable but its direction of custody is unresolved — a single response, an orphan calendar event, a scoresheet with no instrument
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.when: a tender archive, portal export or bid container refuses inspection; the filename's reference token must not manufacture membership
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

sensitivity_why: The posture is MIXED WITHIN ONE GROUP, which is what separates it from the government schema's flat authority-side default. Three populations coexist under a single competition reference and none of them may inherit another's treatment. First, material the authority is under a duty to publish: the contract notice, the issued specification, the award notice. Second, third-party commercial property the authority holds in trust and did not author: received tenders, priced schedules, bidder insurances and named CVs, and — before the deadline — the mere fact of who bid, which the receipt register discloses in a single column. Third, named-person material about people inside and outside the authority: evaluator declarations of interest naming relationships to bidders, moderator narratives about named organisations, and standstill letters whose disclosures are bilateral by construction, since each names the winner and the recipient's own scores and no two are interchangeable. Publication of the award does not retro-publish the file, and an unsuccessful organisation's identity must never surface in a folder label or a model prompt, because the filesystem would then broadcast a defeat that the debrief regime keeps between two parties. Handling classes are P7's; this node records only potentially_sensitive.
open_question: Three items for R1c and Joseph. First, whether a bounded competition key may ever be declared on the government schema; without one this row can recommend no dimension despite an obvious competition-then-function-then-work-type structure, and the same question is already open on government.grant-programme-administration from the funding side — it should be decided once, not twice. Second, whether a body that runs a regulated competition but is not clearly inside the state (a state-owned operator, a utility, a university, an arm's-length delivery company, or a charity buying under a funder's flow-down conditions) activates this row, the government schema at all, or business_operations.procurement-sourcing; the notice-and-procedure evidence is identical in every case and only the body's constitution differs, which is exactly the never-alone problem. Third, whether the supplier side of a regulated competition — a bidder who must respond to notices, meet exclusion grounds, and receive standstill letters — has any home other than business_operations.procurement-sourcing, which the roster frames as a private buyer's sourcing rather than a seller's bid desk; this row cannot hold it and should not be widened to try.
